text.p: - Foreign Minister Davorin Kracun signed a joint declaration on closer cooperation with neighbouring Hungary and Italy in Rome.
- Slovenia expects its association agreement with the European Union to be ratified by the European parliament on Thursday.
- Trade unions will stage a two-hour general strike on Thursday demanding employers refrain from cuts in workers' benefits.
- Petrol refinery Lendava said it would have to shut down unless government lifts petrol prices immediately. The refinery said total losses were approaching two billion tolars ($14.5 million).
- Slovenia's Apartment Fund said it would give another two billion tolars in loans to citizens wanting to buy or build new homes.
- The mayor of the northeastern city of Maribor, Alojz Krizman, asked the government for special protection for him and his family after a series of bomb explosions in the region.
- Slovenia's primary schools will face one of the biggest reforms by the end of the century. The future emphasis will be on Slovene language, mathematics and sports, experts said.
- In the first eight months of the year, 1.2 million tourists visited Slovenia, a five percent increase from the same period in 1995, the country's statistics office said.
- Slovenia's restructuring agency said 751 companies had already completed their privatisation, while another 1,305 were still in the process.
